parsed.explanation: The combined regime creates substantial, documented visitor-facing exposure: national passport restrictions and discrepancy-based entry review can cause questioning, refusal, or—in a nonautomatic but serious case—fraud ineligibility; national rules also restrict access to government-funded single-sex facilities. State/province rules add a ban on gender-affirming care for minors and restrict sports participation, while providing no statewide public-accommodation protection or gender-identity hate-crime coverage. Severe abuse is documented in national immigration and corrections custody, though detention is contingent and the dossier does not establish its likelihood for visitors. The state/province has no current general facility-use ban; its past ban was repealed. This is materially riskier than jurisdictions with only recurring service friction, but the dossier does not document routine arrests of trans visitors, systematic entry detention, or near-certain imprisonment.

entry_documents.exposure: National policy bars new X markers and requires M/F markers based on supporting documents. Officers are instructed to refuse cases with discrepancies or reasonable doubt and may consider a lifetime fraud ineligibility finding if all legal elements are met; this is not automatic. Trans travellers have reported blocked or confiscated passports and being stranded.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X passports remain valid until expiration. The passport policy is challenged in court, but the national court allowed it to take effect. No state/province visitor-document protection is documented.
entry_documents.interaction: The national entry and document regime applies in this state/province. State/province birth certificates must retain the originally assigned sex alongside any change, but the dossier does not establish how this affects visitors’ foreign documents.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections policy includes hormone removal and other measures described as conversion therapy. Trans men in immigration custody reported forced labour, beatings, solitary confinement, and severe sexual abuse. A state/province bathroom arrest and men's-ward placement occurred under an earlier law, but that law was repealed.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: National custody practices apply independently of the state/province’s current lack of a general facility-use ban. State/province law bars public funding for transition care for people in prison.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: National policy bars transgender people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with their identity. The state/province has no current statute barring identity-congruent facility use, but legislators revived a bill in 2025; its text and status are not established.
federal_state_facilities.protection: The 2016 state/province bathroom restriction was repealed in 2017. No current state/province facility-use ban is documented.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: The state/province repeal does not displace the national restriction in facilities governed by national policy. The dossier does not establish its application to every facility a visitor might use.

care_services.exposure: State/province law bars puberty blockers, hormones, and gender-affirming surgery for people under 18, including visiting minors, and bars public funding for transition care for minors and incarcerated people. National funding and care policies add uncertainty; medication import and ordinary emergency-care treatment are not documented.
care_services.interaction: A minor travelling with a guardian may be unable to obtain the specified transition care in this state/province; the parent’s or guardian’s legal exposure is not established. National funding restrictions may further limit access.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National orders characterize gender diversity as a threat and restrict identity-document and facility policies. National counterterrorism strategy names radically pro-transgender groups among priorities, but the reward memorandum does not make trans identity a criterion, and the strategy says mere disagreement will not be targeted.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: National employment and hate-crime protections remain documented, though their practical reach is limited and does not override the described visitor-facing restrictions.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: The national hostile policy operates alongside national protections; those protections do not cancel the document, facility, or custody exposures. No state/province policy targeting trans visitors is documented.

minors_guardians.exposure: State/province law bars specified gender-affirming care for minors and excludes people assigned male at birth from female sports teams. National policy also targets care for minors and directs investigation of schools facilitating social transition, but application to visiting families is not established.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor seeking covered care or competing in a female team faces state/province restrictions. The dossier does not establish that a visiting parent or guardian would be investigated or penalized.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: The dossier gives a recorded killing figure but explicitly says it cannot be compared with the state/province’s general homicide rate; it establishes no violence rate or pattern. State/province hate-crime law excludes gender identity. No current police targeting campaign is documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National gender-identity hate-crime law applies, but state/province bias-crime coverage does not. No visitor-specific evidence of effective police response to anti-trans violence is documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: National protection may offer a legal route, but the state/province gap limits local bias-crime charging. The killing figure is not used as evidence of elevated trans-specific risk without a valid background comparison.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: The passport policy is in force despite litigation; several other national orders are blocked or enjoined. State/province public-accommodation protection is local and covers only part of the population; practical remedies vary by location.
remedies_unknowns.protection: National court challenges and legal-aid guidance are documented, but no completed remedy reversing the passport restriction is shown. Local ordinances provide protection in some places, not statewide.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Which national measures are operative can change, and local protections cannot displace national entry, custody, or facility rules. The 2025 state/province bill’s status and local ordinance coverage at a particular destination are unresolved.

anchor_checks.comparison: This is comparable in having operative identity-based facility restrictions, but the dossier limits the national rule to government-funded single-sex facilities rather than all public buildings. Conversely, this jurisdiction adds national document and entry-screening risks and documented severe custody abuse. The overall exposure is substantial, though the breadth and routine application of each restriction remain less fully established.

This jurisdiction has serious official restrictions and documented custody harms, but unlike the anchor it has no current state/province-wide public-facility ban or documented routine police stops and fraud threats. Its national entry and document rules still create a substantial additional risk; the dossier does not establish routine detention of trans visitors.

It is materially riskier than the anchor: national document restrictions, entry review, facility limits, and custody abuses go beyond inconsistent local service refusals with functioning remedies. The state/province’s uneven local protections and lack of current general facility ban temper, but do not remove, those national exposures.

It is substantially riskier than this reduced-risk anchor, which documents accepted foreign documents, effective lodging remedies, and identity-congruent facility and ward practice. Here national document and facility restrictions are operative, and severe custody harms are documented; no comparable, reliably effective visitor-facing remedy is established.

parsed.synthesis: The operative journey combines national and state/province rules rather than allowing the state/province’s repeal of its former bathroom ban to neutralize national restrictions. A document discrepancy can prompt additional scrutiny or refusal at entry; the stated lifetime fraud consequence requires further legal elements and is not automatic. National facility restrictions and custody practices create additional exposure, with the most severe documented harms arising if a traveller enters immigration or corrections custody. The state/province adds direct constraints for minors seeking specified care and for trans athletes, while local service protections are partial and its hate-crime law omits gender identity. The dossier does not establish routine visitor arrests, the status of the revived facility bill, or the effectiveness of remedies against national policy.
